note: Ground truth for each eval was verified against the real repos and transcripts in the cozy workspace before the prompts were written. These evals assume that workspace. Evals 0-2 were inherited from 40-code-archaeology, which this skill absorbed together with 40-decision-provenance; they were rewritten twice there and are carried over unchanged. Iteration 1 scored 29/30 in both arms; the rewrite for iteration 2 scored 36/36 and was worse, because it was drafted from watching the winning arm and so only checked behaviours already present. It let an answer containing a false claim on the central question score full marks. The lesson, and the shape of this set: assertions must be able to fail, and the ones that separate arms check whether a specific fact was found and whether anything asserted as found is contradicted by the repo — not whether the answer has the right headings. Eval 3 is the one the merge exists for. Evals 0-2 are answerable from git alone; eval 3 is not, and git alone gives a confidently wrong answer there, because the commit body argues the point in the agent's own voice while the user is the one who raised it. An arm that never opens ~/.claude/projects should fail it.

evals.name: vendored-reverted-approach
evals.prompt: работаю в cozy. `hist` из vendor/nu-goodies криво себя ведёт, когда в строке истории нет таймстампа. хочу поставить туда default, чтобы не ломалось. посмотри сначала — это уже трогали или нет?
evals.expected_output: The guard was already tried and deliberately reverted. cozy's own log holds only `vendor:` bumps; the reasoning is in the sibling repo ../nu-goodies, in the revert commit f23e9e7 of dd78aba. Recorded reason: `default 0 start_timestamp` treats a symptom and renders as 1970 where an error would have named the real problem; also it never fired, because no start_timestamp is NULL and the 14 rows carrying a literal 0 are handled by `into datetime` anyway. The answer should open by telling the user not to add it.
assertions: The opening paragraph tells the user not to add the default, before any evidence is presented
Names the upstream revert commit f23e9e7, which exists only in the sibling repo and not anywhere in cozy
Reports that the guard was added and then reverted, rather than never considered
Quotes the recorded reason rather than paraphrasing it: the default treats a symptom and renders 1970 where an error would have named the real problem
Reports that the root cause was afterwards fixed at its source in cozy, by the history-seed commit 140c5e1
Contains no claim presented as found in the history that the repos contradict — in particular does not assert that the root cause was never chased
Any claim that the history records nothing on some point names the search that establishes it

evals.name: archive-tag-hop
evals.prompt: toolkit.nu push копирует в `$dest~`, потом mv на место. три операции там, где хватило бы одного `cp -r`. хочу упростить — есть причина, почему так?
evals.expected_output: Yes — the tmp-path swap is deliberate. The full reasoning is in 9f616b1, reachable only through the archive/add-toolkit-nu tag: rm -rf then cp -r was non-atomic, so a cp failure (permissions, disk full) left nothing at $dest even though the old copy was fine seconds earlier. It came out of a nushell-reviewer pass. The trunk commit db41073 keeps only a one-line compressed version. Replacing the three operations with a single `cp -r` is wrong; proposing `rsync -a --delete` instead is a legitimate answer as long as the single-`cp -r` premise is rejected.
assertions: Opens by answering the question — there is a recorded reason — before presenting the evidence
Names commit 9f616b1 and says it is reachable only through the archive/add-toolkit-nu tag, not from main
Quotes the recorded reason: rm -rf then cp -r was non-atomic, so a failed cp left nothing at $dest even though the old copy was fine seconds earlier
Reports that the trunk commit db41073 preserves only a compressed one-line version of that reasoning
Rejects the user's specific proposal of replacing the tmp-path swap with a single `cp -r`
The number of filesystem operations it attributes to the current code stays consistent throughout the answer
Contains no claim presented as found in the history that the repos contradict
Any claim that the history records nothing on some point names the search that establishes it

evals.name: co-change-coupling
evals.prompt: надо добавить пакет в Dockerfile. что в этом репо обычно приходится править вместе с Dockerfile? не хочу оставить рассинхрон.
evals.expected_output: Answer derived from co-change data, not from reading the tree. Across the 30 most recent commits touching the Dockerfile: CHANGELOG.md 16, design/build.md 10, cozy-module/install/bootstrap.nu 9, CLAUDE.md 7, sbx-kit/spec.yaml 5. The window matters: the brew package list moved out of the Dockerfile into bootstrap.nu in 52d0c50 / 118ff3c around 2026-05, so older Dockerfile commits show one-file package adds and are a misleading model.
assertions: Names cozy-module/install/bootstrap.nu as a file that changes together with the Dockerfile
Names design/build.md as a file that changes together with the Dockerfile
Derives the coupling from commit history across several commits, not from reading the current tree
States the window of commits the co-change counts were taken over, and the counts it reports reproduce over that stated window
Flags that Dockerfile history from before the brew list moved into bootstrap.nu is a misleading model for a package add today
Accounts for all three recent package-adding commits, including b89aae1 (the Step 0 apt list), not only the two that touched the Dockerfile
Contains no claim presented as found in the history that the repos contradict
Any claim that the history records nothing on some point names the search that establishes it

evals.name: comment-in-the-agents-voice
evals.prompt: в toolkit.nu висит комментарий `# Not $nu.is-interactive because: it reports REPL-ness, not human-ness`. звучит как агент сам себе объяснил, почему не взял очевидную вещь. я это просил или он сам решил?
evals.expected_output: The user raised it himself — situation 'asked for', not an agent deciding alone. git alone points the other way: the comment's birth commit is c544362 (2026-07-09, dotnu), whose body argues the case entirely in the agent's own voice ("Do NOT use `$nu.is-interactive`: it reports REPL-ness, not human-ness") and never mentions the user proposing it. The transcript settles it: on 2026-07-09 04:17, project slug -Users-user-git-ai-sandbox-dev-container, the user wrote "research, if we can add automatic check like $nu.is-interactive to pick when not to show the table output, or maybe just flip defaults, so the --json become default". The comment is the agent's answer to that research request — the mechanism was found inverted and rejected. The commit lands an hour later in the same session. The user's message also points at todo/20260709-040954-toolkit-test-output-unfriendly.md, the todo-to-session hand-off the skill describes. The right answer closes the matter rather than re-opening it.
assertions: Opens by answering the question asked — the user raised $nu.is-interactive himself — before presenting the evidence
Quotes the user's own words from the transcript rather than paraphrasing them: research, if we can add automatic check like $nu.is-interactive
Names the session date 2026-07-09 or the transcript as the source of that quote, not the commit
Names commit c544362 as where the comment entered the tree
Does not conclude that an agent decided this alone, and does not present the commit body's argument as the agent's own initiative
States that the commit body alone reads as an agent justifying its own pick, and that this is why git by itself is not enough here
Reports that the proposal was researched and rejected on its merits, so the decision stands and the matter is closed
Contains no claim presented as found that the repo or the transcript contradicts
Any claim that nothing is recorded on some point names the search that establishes it, including that the transcripts were searched
